analysis: The method checks if the provided index is within bounds (0 <= index < size). If not, it throws an IndexOutOfBoundsException to signal an invalid argument. The method then proceeds to remove and return the element at the valid index, adjusting the internal array accordingly. The exception is thrown immediately upon detecting an invalid index, preventing further execution and alerting the caller of the misuse.
answer: The programmer did not expect the runtime exception to be caught externally; it is an unchecked exception indicating a programming error (invalid index) that should propagate up the call stack to highlight the bug.
remark: The exception is thrown when the index parameter is greater than or equal to size, which indicates an out-of-bounds access attempt. This is a typical preconditions check in collection implementations, and the exception serves as a clear signal of incorrect usage rather than a recoverable condition.
